components.text: Intangible cultural heritage means the traditional cultural expressions that people of all ethnic groups have passed down through generations and regard as part of their cultural heritage, together with the objects and places associated with them.
components.attribution: ICH Law of the PRC, Article 2 (translated)

notes: What counts as intangible cultural heritage? Start with the law. Article 2 of China's Intangible Cultural Heritage Law, in force since June 2011, defines it as the traditional cultural expressions that people of all ethnic groups have passed down through generations and regard as part of their cultural heritage, together with the objects and places associated with them. Three things follow. It is handed down, not newly invented. The community itself sees it as its own. And it is not only the performance or the skill, but also the objects and places that go with it: the leather figures of a shadow play, an opera stage, the carved blocks for New Year prints. The same article lists the fields: oral literature and the languages that carry it, fine arts, calligraphy, music, dance, drama, storytelling and acrobatics, craftsmanship, medicine and calendars, rituals, festivals and other customs, and traditional sports and games. The quotation is my translation.
